column1: # jobleft industries: the words that name an industry in a job posting, in an employer's name, and how close two
# industries are.
# Source: written new for jobleft by the match lane (2026-09-25). First-party data; no third-party list was copied.
# Licence: same as the jobleft project.
# Format: id | name | strong phrases | weak phrases | employer-name phrases | related industries (id:weight)
#   * strong: one phrase in the posting's own words is enough to name the industry (3 points).
#   * weak: 1 point each; an industry is named at 3 points, so three different weak phrases, or one weak phrase and
#     a strong one. Every phrase counts once, however often it repeats.
#   * Phrases are matched longest first across every industry, so "food bank" is a nonprofit and never a bank.
#   * employer-name phrases: words in an employer's name that name its industry ("Austin ISD", "Mercy Hospital").
#     When a name holds several, the one nearest the end wins ("Texas Tech University" is a university).
#   * Only the parts of a posting that describe the employer and the work are read. Requirement lists, benefits and
#     equal-opportunity text are skipped ("health insurance" is a benefit, "high school diploma" is a requirement).
#   * related weight: how much experience in one industry counts for the other (1 = same). Pairs are symmetric.
